name: Khaki olive
lede: Khaki olive is a moderate, yellowish brown named for the olive, and it is among the most common named colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: An olive, not a dust color
sections.body:
The color library files Khaki olive from RAL, dated 1927, with no plate or hue note attached [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[greyish-brown]] and [[bronze]], at 
In LCH terms it measures lightness 44, chroma 22, hue 90 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "moderate yellowish brown" block, Munsell 4.5Y 4.3/3.1 [1]. This color is not carried in our color library's wider cross-reference set, so we cannot give it a precise nearest named neighbor here [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 4,828 of 23,781 paintings, 20.3 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 2,774 [2]. That makes it more common than 98 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1700s, at 13.1 percent of that century's 3,449 paintings, 1.1 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a light, in 31 percent of its appearances [2].

Salomon van Ruysdael is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 7 of his 13 works here, 3.4 times the baseline [2]. The earliest match is dated 900, by Zhao Guangfu; that is 1,027 years before the name's own first record, in 1927, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence of the actual paint, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases with [[water-grey|Water Grey]] and [[indigo-tea|Indigo tea]] more than chance would predict [2].

origin.named_after: pairs khaki, a word for dust-colored cloth, with olive; the pairing itself is undocumented
